varieties.name: Pink jasmine (J. polyanthum)
varieties.note: The one sold in bud in winter. It needs four to six weeks of cool nights, around 10-13 °C, in autumn to set buds: kept warm all year it makes leaves and no flowers.

varieties.name: Arabian jasmine (J. sambac)
varieties.note: Tropical and warmth-loving: it flowers through the heat of summer and wants no cool period. The least cold-tolerant of them; keep it above 13 °C.

varieties.name: Common jasmine (J. officinale)
varieties.note: The hardiest, and summer-flowering. Happiest with a cool, drier winter rest, after which it flowers on new growth.

varieties.name: Spanish jasmine (J. grandiflorum)
varieties.note: Long flowering and tender, grown for its scent. Treated as J. officinale but kept warmer.

varieties.name: Angel-wing jasmine (J. nitidum)
varieties.note: Shrubbier than the climbers and tender. It flowers on new growth, so prune after a flush rather than before one.

watering.label: Keep evenly moist while in leaf; a full dry-out costs the buds

drainage.label: Moisture-retentive mix that still drains; a flowering vine drinks faster than it looks

young: Too dark. A young plant needs light to build the wood it will flower on.
Dim. Expect reaching growth; flowering is not the question at this age.
A little short for its age, so it will take longer to reach flowering size.
established: Too dark. Few flowers or none, and long reaching growth between leaves.
Dim. Foliage carries on; buds are unlikely to set.
A little short. It will flower sparsely rather than freely.
Burning. Leaves yellow and drop, with crisp brown margins.
Too much. Even a sun-lover bleaches at this level if the pot runs dry.
Far too much. Leaf loss rather than leaf damage.
